claim:
For the square-lattice nonreversal quantum walk of arXiv:1303.1966, choose the admissible coin parameters \(\lambda=1/\sqrt2\), \(\gamma=0\), with all six phases zero. The resulting \(SU(4)\) coin preserves \(\operatorname{span}\{|x+\rangle,|y-\rangle\}\), and its restriction to that sector is the standard Hadamard coin. Let \(X_t\) and \(Y_t\) denote the two lattice coordinates after \(t\) steps. Starting from the origin with coin state \(|x+\rangle\),
\[
\lim_{t\to\infty}\frac{\mathbb E[X_t^2]}{t^2}=1-\frac{3\sqrt2}{8},
\]
whereas starting from the origin with coin state \(|y-\rangle\),
\[
\lim_{t\to\infty}\frac{\mathbb E[X_t^2]}{t^2}=\frac{\sqrt2}{8}.
\]
The difference is \(1-1/\sqrt2>0\). Hence the paper's numerically motivated conjecture that every even-total-degree joint moment of the nonreversal walk is independent of the initial coin state is false, already for the degree-two moment \(\mathbb E[X_t^2]\) at its leading ballistic coefficient. The claim is limited to this admissible boundary subfamily \(\gamma=0\); it does not assert failure for Haar-generic or strictly interior nonreversal coins.

integrity.computational_role: Finite exact checks verify the coin algebra and finite-time reflection identities; they are not used as a substitute for the asymptotic proof.
integrity.prior_work_preserved: The source nonrepeating theorem and the classical one-dimensional Hadamard weak-limit theorem are not claimed as new.
integrity.proof_basis: Exact invariant-subspace reduction plus an analytic Fourier weak-limit moment calculation.

scientific_limitations: The counterexample uses the admissible boundary subfamily \(\gamma=0\); no generic or strictly interior failure is claimed.
Only the degree-two Cartesian moment \(\mathbb E[X_t^2]\) is needed and proved to violate initial-state independence.
The one-dimensional Hadamard weak limit is prior work and is used solely as a reduction tool.
title: An invariant Hadamard sector disproves initial-state independence for a nonreversal quantum walk
